items.notes: ACL note affirms that the layer owns mapping and names layer-level SPOF/resilience risks, but it does not state the risk of mappings with no owner.
Option A covers module isolation, contracts and dependency direction; it does not address read models, consistency or replacing a synchronous dependency.
HTTP method and idempotency semantics explain retry safety, not how a client retrieves submitted-job status after a lost acknowledgment.
Directly names the xDS management server and EDS endpoint discovery path that must exist for Envoy to fetch cluster endpoints.
Decision text requires either a known part count or an explicit release rule or expiry recording a partial or forced result instead of silent success.
Claim-check decision requires payload lifecycle and failure-handling owners but does not describe the failure caused by publishing a token before durable payload storage.
Explains that the outbox records publication intent in the same local transaction and a relay publishes it, with at-least-once redelivery.
States explicitly that a relay may send a message more than once, which is the reason consumers must tolerate duplicate publication.
Contrasts refresh with eviction and notes that a stored value can be served during asynchronous reload, but does not say when TTL expiration alone breaks the freshness promise.
Describes write-then-invalidate mechanics and brief post-write staleness, but not the dependency on reliable change signaling.
